subject: VPC pricing: amortization, implementation credit and SLA split
messages:
From: Claire Ramos <claire.ramos@clearpointhealth.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Cc: legal@clearpointhealth.com
Date: 2027-03-22T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: VPC pricing: amortization, implementation credit and SLA split

Hi Grace,

Thanks for the demo last week — the team was impressed with the latency guarantees and the KV caching approach. Procurement is pulling together the commercial ask and we have three quick items we need clarity on before we engage legal: 

1) Platform fee amortization: Is the platform fee billed up front or can Clearpoint amortize it over the committed term on the SOW/invoice? Our finance team prefers amortization for capex budgeting.
2) Implementation credits: We have a 6–8 month rollout window (multi-site). Would Redwood consider an implementation credit that offsets the platform fee in year one if we take a 24-month committed term?
3) SLA & oncall split: We need an explicit split between product/platform SLA credits vs. oncall engineering (3rd line) commitments — i.e., how do credits apply if onprem infra vs. Redwood-managed control plane?

Can you share a short MAAP (mutual action plan) and a straw commercial that reflects those options? Goal is to have something to show legal by next Tuesday.

Appreciate it —
Claire Ramos
Procurement Manager
Clearpoint Health

(attachment: procurement_requirements_summary.pdf stub)

From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
To: Claire Ramos <claire.ramos@clearpointhealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-03-22T12:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: VPC pricing: amortization, implementation credit and SLA split

Hi Claire — great to hear from you and glad the demo resonated. Quick responses below and attaching a one‑pager MAAP and a straw commercial for the 24‑month commit: Redwood_VPC_Term_Summary.pdf (attached).

1) Platform fee amortization: We can support amortization on the invoice level for accounting purposes — the commercial will show the platform fee as a single line but we can issue a monthly amortization-friendly invoice schedule or a payment plan on a 24‑month term. For customers who prefer capitalizing, we provide an invoice addendum that states the fee is for a multi‑year entitlement.

2) Implementation credit: We can offer an implementation credit that offsets up to 75% of the platform fee in year one for a 24‑month committed deal with a minimum reserved capacity. Typical structure we propose: a $75k implementation credit applied as a one‑time credit on the first invoice, contingent on a signed SOW and 24‑month master commitment. This credit is non‑refundable and amortized on our side across the first 12 months for accounting.

3) SLA & oncall split: For Private (VPC/on‑prem) deployments we separate: 
  - Platform SLA (control plane availability, API routing, model fallback): credits under the platform SLA.
  - Oncall/ops response (customer infra, on‑prem node health): handled via the support tier.

Our standard approach: Enterprise Plus support includes 24/7 oncall (1‑hour P0 response), a monthly ops runbook review, and oncall escalation into our SREs. If Clearpoint operates the on‑prem nodes, platform credits still apply for control plane failures; operational issues tied to customer hardware are handled under the support retainer and won’t automatically trigger platform credits. We can define hybrid carveouts in the SOW if you need specific pass‑throughs.

I've attached a short MAAP (Clearpoint_MAAP_v1.xlsx) that maps milestones and the credit trigger points. Can we schedule a 30‑minute sync tomorrow to review with legal and engineering?

Best,
Grace O'Connor

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-03-22T14:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: VPC pricing: amortization, implementation credit and SLA split

Looping in a few technical clarifications that we should bake into the commercial/SOW: 

- Node licensing and failover: If Clearpoint requires on‑prem nodes with cross‑region failover to our hosted control plane, we should specify licensing transfer rights (how a reserved node moves between sites) and whether a transient failover will count towards usage. Recommend a clause: transient failover grace of 72 hours before additional consumption billing.

- Implementation credit mechanics: Instead of a straight platform fee offset, propose splitting credits: $50k implementation credit + $25k performance tuning credit tied to a post‑go‑live latency benchmark (30 days). This protects Redwood against scope creep and ties credit to measurable tuning deliverables.

- SLA split examples to include in SOW: table of failure modes (control-plane, model serving, customer infra) and which party owns remediation + credit path. Also include an optional 3‑month ramp credit (pro‑rated usage credit) for the first quarter of production — useful for smoothing early over‑run usage.

I'll draft the short technical attachment for tomorrow's call (MAAP appendix).

—Ben
Ben Carter
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

• We prefer the credit to be applied against the platform fee line item rather than invoiced separately; does Redwood need the credit to be amortized internally or can it appear as a straight deduction on the first invoice?

• For the performance tuning credit, can you define the latency SLA and measurement windows so legal can include objective acceptance criteria (example: p95 inference latency < 150ms measured over 7 consecutive days)?

• Timeline: we need the MAAP + straw commercial by COB Friday to present to the CFO next week. Can you confirm?

Claire

Claire — confirmed. We will: 
1) Show the implementation credit as a direct deduction on the first invoice (not a separate line) for clarity to your finance team; Redwood will internally amortize for accounting but the customer invoice will reflect the net.
2) For the performance tuning credit we will set objective criteria: p95 inference latency < 150ms over a 7‑day rolling window measured on production traffic, and a baseline capture period of 14 days post‑deploy to avoid noisy early results. The $25k credit will trigger after a 30‑day tuning window following go‑live.
3) MAAP & straw commercial: delivering both by COB Friday — attaching updated MAAP and a commercial term summary in the HubSpot link.

Next steps: I’ll run the updated MAAP by legal internally and then we can jump on a 30 minute call Friday at 10:00am PT if that works for you to finalize language for the SOW.
